(2) Outside the obesity pool this asset already prices: NCHS Data Brief 516 (Gwira, Fryar, Gu, November 2024, NHANES August 2021 to August 2023, adults 20 and over) gives diagnosed diabetes in 5.2% of adults with BMI under 25, 9.5% at BMI 25 to 29.9 and 16.3% at BMI 30 or more; weighted by the same survey's BMI bands as the book holds them (obesity 40.3%, data/epidemiology.csv; overweight 86,594,086 of 266,978,268 adults = 32.43%, NCHS Health E-Stat 111, data/epidemiology.csv; the remaining 27.27% under 25), 59.35% of adults with diagnosed diabetes have BMI 30 or more, 27.84% are at 25 to 29.9 and 12.81% under 25. 0.495 x (1 - 0.5935) = 0.2012, a pool of 5,432,832 adults

Its anchor: GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors together reached 13.3% of medicated US adults with type 2 diabetes in NHANES 2017 to March 2020 (Mittman BG et al., Curr Med Res Opin 2024;40(3):377-383, doi:10.1080/03007995.2024.2303413), one product in one of the two classes read at about a seventh of that two-class share
column12: one rate for every incretin claimant in this pool rather than a new judgement per asset. Leans high for a late entrant against semaglutide, tirzepatide and orforglipron already holding the class; leans low in that this slice now carries the overweight band, where weight loss is wanted more than in Foundayo's lean slice. No measured analogue was used.
